name: Tabimorelin

angle.text: Listed alongside other growth hormone secretagogues, tabimorelin is discussed as an oral route to higher growth hormone and thereby better body composition. It was studied in a few early human trials for hormone release, and no appearance or body-composition outcome has been tested.

summary: Early experimental oral GH secretagogue; a few early human studies and no appearance data.
note: Experimental only; inhibits CYP3A4, so drug interactions are possible.
currentQuick:
Tabimorelin is an experimental oral drug from the first generation of growth hormone secretagogues. It was tested in healthy men and in adults with growth hormone deficiency.
It raised growth hormone and IGF-1, but clinical benefit was limited and it was never approved.
How it works: It mimics ghrelin at the GH secretagogue receptor to trigger growth hormone release.
Risks and caveats: It inhibits the liver enzyme CYP3A4, creating potential interactions with other drugs. Human data are limited to a few early studies.
deepLead:
Tabimorelin (NN703) is an experimental, orally active growth hormone secretagogue that was among the earlier compounds in its class. It acts on the ghrelin receptor to stimulate growth hormone release.
Published human studies are early-phase work in healthy men, an interaction study with the CYP3A4 substrate midazolam, and work in growth hormone-deficient adults. It is not approved for any use. No studies have tested it for appearance purposes.

name: GHRP-1

angle.text: GHRP-1 is an early growth hormone releasing peptide that bodybuilding and peptide communities group with GHRP-6 and GHRP-2 as a way to raise growth hormone for muscle and fat loss. Some 1990s human work measured hormone release; body-composition or appearance outcomes have not been tested.

summary: Early research growth hormone releasing peptide; some 1990s human data and no appearance evidence.
note: Research peptide; not an approved medicine; prohibited in sport.
currentQuick:
GHRP-1 is one of the first synthetic growth hormone releasing peptides, developed alongside GHRP-6 and GHRP-2.
It was given to people in early studies and releases growth hormone, but it was never approved and no study has examined it for appearance.
How it works: It binds the ghrelin/GH secretagogue receptor, separate from the GHRH receptor, prompting growth hormone release.
Risks and caveats: It is not approved as a medicine, and little modern human safety data exists. Anti-doping labs test for it.
deepLead:
GHRP-1 (growth hormone releasing peptide-1) is a synthetic peptide from the first family of growth hormone releasing peptides, which also includes GHRP-6 and GHRP-2. These small peptides of six to seven amino acids stimulate growth hormone release through a receptor distinct from the GHRH receptor.
A 1993 review reported that GHRP-6, GHRP-1 and GHRP-2 were the three such peptides given to humans, in increasing order of effectiveness, and that all released more growth hormone than GHRH 1-44. GHRP-1 is not approved as a medicine. Anti-doping laboratories have developed urine tests for it and its metabolites.
No clinical trials in healthy people for appearance were found.

name: Alexamorelin

angle.text: Alexamorelin is an obscure hexarelin-related peptide that appears in growth hormone secretagogue lists, where the draw is more growth hormone for muscle and fat loss. A 2000 study reported its endocrine effects in humans, and it is mostly known from anti-doping screening; appearance outcomes are untested.

summary: An obscure hexarelin-related GH secretagogue peptide known mostly from anti-doping screening papers; no appearance trials exist.
note: Not an approved medicine; listed in doping-control peptide panels.
currentQuick:
Alexamorelin is a lab-made peptide that stimulates growth hormone release, related to hexarelin. It is discussed mainly in sports anti-doping research.
One 2000 human study described its hormonal effects; no study has tested it for muscle or looks outcomes.
How it works: As a growth hormone secretagogue, it is described as raising the body's own GH output rather than supplying GH itself [3].
Risks and caveats: No safety data from clinical trials were found. It is covered by sports drug-testing screens and is not an approved drug.
deepLead:
Alexamorelin is a synthetic heptapeptide growth hormone secretagogue, related to hexarelin, with the sequence Ala-His-D-2-methyl-Trp-Ala-Trp-D-Phe-Lys-NH2. A 2000 study reported its endocrine activities in humans .
It has not been approved as a medicine. It appears in the scientific literature mainly as one of the growth hormone releasing peptides (GHRPs) that anti-doping laboratories screen for in urine . It is named among the prohibited peptides covered by sports drug-testing methods .
No published trials have tested it for any appearance or muscle-related outcome.

name: Deslorelin

chain: Change in puberty-linked growth and looks
angle.text: Deslorelin is a veterinary GnRH-agonist implant that appears on hormone-focused lists because GnRH agonists shift sex-hormone output. Pediatric endocrine research on related drugs exists, while use of deslorelin itself for appearance is untested and rests on anecdote.

summary: A veterinary GnRH-agonist implant with some pediatric endocrine research; nothing tests it for looks.
note: Veterinary drug; not approved for general human use.
currentQuick:
Deslorelin is a lab-made GnRH agonist mostly sold for animals, such as implants that suppress fertility in dogs and ferrets or trigger ovulation in horses.
In humans it appears in older research on precocious puberty and other endocrine conditions. No studies address appearance or muscle use.
How it works: It acts on the pituitary GnRH receptor; continuous exposure suppresses reproductive hormones after an initial surge [3].
Risks and caveats: Human safety data come from specialist trials in children and patients. It is not approved for general human use, and the veterinary product Ovuplant was withdrawn in the US after fertility-timing problems in mares [1].
deepLead:
Deslorelin is a synthetic gonadotropin-releasing hormone (GnRH) superagonist used mainly in veterinary medicine, sold under names such as Suprelorin, Ovuplant and Sucromate Equine . It is used to control reproduction in animals, for example to induce ovulation in mares and as a slow-release implant for reversible contraception in dogs and ferrets .
In humans it has been studied in research settings, including long-term treatment of children with precocious puberty . It is not approved for general human use . No studies have examined it for appearance outcomes.

name: Ganirelix

angle.text: Ganirelix is an IVF drug that rapidly suppresses LH and FSH, which is why it is mentioned in hormone-manipulation discussions in muscle and physique circles. Its appearance use is theoretical and untested, with the clinical evidence all coming from fertility treatment.

summary: A GnRH-antagonist fertility drug for IVF; its place on a looks list rests on hormone suppression, not any appearance trial.
note: Prescription IVF drug; no appearance or muscle studies.
currentQuick:
Ganirelix is a prescription injection used during IVF to stop the body ovulating too early.
It is well studied in randomized fertility trials, but no study tests it for appearance or muscle goals.
How it works: It blocks GnRH receptors on the pituitary, quickly lowering LH and FSH; the effect reverses after stopping [2].
Risks and caveats: Reported effects include injection-site reactions, abdominal pain, headache and nausea; it is not for use in pregnancy, and it is Rx-only [2].
deepLead:
Ganirelix, sold as Orgalutran and Antagon among other names, is an injectable GnRH antagonist used in assisted reproduction to prevent premature ovulation during ovarian stimulation for IVF . It competitively blocks pituitary GnRH receptors, rapidly suppressing LH and FSH, with the effect reversing after stopping .
Randomized trials in women undergoing ovarian stimulation compared it with GnRH agonist protocols . It is a prescription fertility drug; no studies examine it for appearance or muscle outcomes.

name: Humanin

angle.text: Humanin is promoted in longevity circles as a mitochondrial peptide that could slow aging, which people connect to staying youthful-looking. The research is in cells and animals, with no human treatment trials and nothing testing skin or other visible aging.

summary: A mitochondria-derived peptide with cell and animal research behind it, and no human trials as a treatment.
note: Research peptide; some studies report tumor-promoting effects in cancer models.
currentQuick:
Humanin is a small peptide made from mitochondrial DNA, discovered in 2001 during Alzheimer research.
Lab and animal work links it to cell survival and insulin action. No human trials have tested it as a treatment or for looks or longevity.
How it works: It is reported to block apoptosis by interfering with Bax [3] and to act on cell-surface receptors including formyl peptide receptors [4].
Risks and caveats: No human safety data from treatment trials were found; some research reports it may impair chemotherapy and promote tumor growth in cancer models [1]. It is not an approved drug.
deepLead:
Humanin is a short peptide encoded within mitochondrial DNA, in the gene for 16S ribosomal RNA, and was the first mitochondria-derived peptide identified . It was discovered in 2001 by several groups studying different questions, including protection of neurons against Alzheimer-related toxicity , interaction with the apoptosis protein Bax  and with IGFBP-3 .
Laboratory and animal research has linked it to cell protection, insulin sensitivity and inflammation . It is not an approved drug; the studies found are cell, animal and observational human work, and no trials were found of humanin as a treatment or for appearance.

name: Dihexa

angle.text: Dihexa is an experimental peptide taken up by nootropic users for memory and learning, which some tie to study and work performance. It has been studied in rodents for memory, has no published human trials, and no appearance link has been tested.

summary: An experimental angiotensin IV-derived peptide studied in rodents for memory; it has no published human trials and no link to appearance.
note: No human data; long half-life in rats has prompted theoretical c-Met-related tumor concerns.
currentQuick:
Dihexa is a laboratory-made peptide derived from angiotensin IV, designed to resist breakdown and cross the blood-brain barrier. It has been studied in rodents for memory impairment and in an Alzheimer mouse model.
It is sold as a research chemical and discussed as a nootropic. No human clinical trial has been published, and it is not an appearance compound.
How it works: Reported to bind hepatocyte growth factor and potentiate signalling through the c-Met receptor, promoting synapse formation in cell cultures; a 2021 mouse study linked its effects to the PI3K/AKT pathway.
Risks and caveats: Human safety is unknown. Authors have raised the theoretical concern that sustained c-Met activation could promote tumors. It is not an approved drug.
deepLead:
Dihexa is a synthetic oligopeptide analog of angiotensin IV, modified to be more stable and to penetrate the brain . It emerged from work on angiotensin IV analogs as potential antidementia agents .
Preclinical studies report that angiotensin IV-derived peptides act through the hepatocyte growth factor/c-Met system , and a 2021 study reported that dihexa rescued cognitive impairment in the APP/PS1 Alzheimer mouse model . No human clinical trials have been published.

name: Selank

angle.text: Forum users group selank with Semax as an anxiolytic nootropic for calmer social situations and better focus, which they connect to a more confident presence. Human evidence is a handful of Russian-language studies on anxiety, and appearance effects have not been studied.

summary: A Russian-developed anxiolytic peptide that forum users group with Semax as a nootropic; human evidence is limited to a few Russian-language studies.
note: Approved only in Russia; products sold elsewhere are unregulated research chemicals.
currentQuick:
Selank is a synthetic seven-amino-acid peptide derived from tuftsin, developed in Russia and registered there as nasal drops for anxiety. On looksmax.org it is discussed alongside Semax and Cerebrolysin as a nootropic, with members asking whether such peptides are "cope".
It has no connection to physical appearance; its place in the community is as a cognition and mood supplement. Published research is mostly animal and in-vitro work, much of it from Russian groups.
How it works: Studies in cells and animals suggest it may influence GABA-related gene expression and inhibit enkephalin-degrading enzymes, which researchers propose as routes to its anxiolytic effects.
Risks and caveats: It is a registered drug only in Russia. Outside Russia it is sold as a research chemical without regulatory oversight. A 2021 pharmacology review grouped it among agents acting on GABA receptors.
deepLead:
Selank is a synthetic heptapeptide (Thr-Lys-Pro-Arg-Pro-Gly-Pro) designed as a longer-lasting analog of tuftsin, a tetrapeptide fragment of immunoglobulin G. It was developed at the Institute of Molecular Genetics of the Russian Academy of Sciences together with the Zakusov Institute of Pharmacology .
Reference works describe it as having been registered in Russia in 2009 as intranasal drops for generalized anxiety disorder . Published studies include animal behavioural experiments and biochemical work on enkephalin-degrading enzymes and GABAergic gene expression .
Within looksmaxxing communities, Selank is discussed as a nootropic, usually together with Semax. No published trial has examined it for appearance outcomes.

name: Cerebrolysin

angle.text: Cerebrolysin is an injectable peptide mixture approved for stroke and dementia in many countries, and forum users discuss it as an iqmaxxing nootropic for study performance. Trials address stroke and dementia, while any appearance link is not drawn or tested.

summary: A porcine brain-derived peptide mixture approved for stroke and dementia in many countries, discussed by forum users as an "iqmaxxing" nootropic.
note: Injectable prescription product; nootropic use in healthy people is not studied.
currentQuick:
Cerebrolysin is an injectable mixture of low-molecular-weight peptides and amino acids prepared from porcine brain protein. It is marketed by EVER Neuro Pharma in Austria and used in many countries as an adjunct for stroke, brain injury and dementia.
On looksmax.org it appears in threads about "iqmaxxing" and "brainmaxxing", where members ask whether it helps studying or exams. It is not an appearance compound, and no studies have tested it in healthy people for cognition.
How it works: Preclinical studies report that it mimics neurotrophic factor activity and promotes neurogenesis in rodent stroke and Alzheimer models, including through the Sonic hedgehog pathway.
Risks and caveats: Human trials are in patients with neurological disease. Being an animal-derived injectable, it is a prescription product where approved; members mention obtaining it from unofficial sources.
deepLead:
Cerebrolysin is a mixture of low-molecular-weight peptides and free amino acids produced by enzymatic breakdown of porcine brain proteins, described as mimicking neurotrophic factors . It is manufactured by EVER Neuro Pharma in Austria and given by injection or infusion .
It is approved in many countries for neurological conditions such as stroke, traumatic brain injury and dementia . Human trials have been conducted in post-stroke recovery, including the CARS randomized trial and a meta-analysis of nine randomized trials .
In looksmaxxing communities it is discussed as a cognitive enhancer. No trial has examined it for appearance outcomes; one small registered study listed hair repigmentation during therapy .

name: Noopept (Omberacetam)

angle.text: Noopept is taken as a nootropic for memory, focus and mood, and in appearance forums it appears in stacks aimed at productivity. Small human studies exist for cognition, and no appearance outcome has been tested.

summary: A Russian-developed racetam-like nootropic with small human studies and no appearance evidence.
note: Unapproved drug in the US; long-term human safety data are lacking.
currentQuick:
Noopept is a synthetic nootropic developed in Russia and sold online as a supplement in many countries. It is chemically related to the racetams.
It is discussed in these communities as a mental-performance compound; no source links it to changes in appearance.
How it works: Laboratory studies suggest antioxidant effects, reduced excitotoxicity and raised growth factors such as BDNF in rodents. Human mechanisms are not well characterised.
Risks and caveats: Long-term human safety studies have not been published. It is an unapproved new drug in the US, prescription-only in Australia and registered as a medicine in Russia.
deepLead:
Noopept, also called omberacetam or GVS-111, is a synthetic dipeptide-like compound promoted as a nootropic (cognitive enhancer). Chemically it is N-phenylacetyl-L-prolylglycine ethyl ester, and it is described as a prodrug of the endogenous dipeptide cycloprolylglycine; it is related to the racetam family. It was developed by Russian pharmacology researchers, including T. A. Gudasheva and S. B. Seredenin, and its synthesis was first reported in 1996.
It is registered as a medicine in Russia, while in the United States it is an unapproved "new drug" that the FDA has treated as a piracetam analog, and it is nonetheless sold online as a supplement. Its interest in looksmaxxing-adjacent communities is as a "mental" or recovery compound rather than as an appearance treatment; no source examined links it to any change in physical appearance.
Published work consists mostly of laboratory and animal studies of neuroprotection, plus a small number of Russian clinical comparisons with piracetam. Human evidence is limited, and Wikipedia notes that no long-term studies of chronic use exist.

name: Coluracetam

angle.text: Coluracetam is a racetam sold as a nootropic for focus and mood, drawing on its development for Alzheimer's and depression. Appearance use is not drawn by users, and its evidence base is the abandoned pharma programs.

summary: An abandoned pharma racetam sold as a nootropic, with no appearance evidence.
note: Never approved; development discontinued.
currentQuick:
Coluracetam is an experimental racetam developed by a Japanese drug company, tested for Alzheimer's and depression, and later sold online as a nootropic.
No source links it to appearance.
How it works: It increases choline uptake in rodent brain tissue, raising acetylcholine synthesis; AMPA-related effects have also been suggested.
Risks and caveats: No approved use; side-effect data are not described in the sources reviewed. Prescription-only in Australia.
deepLead:
Coluracetam (also MKC-231 or BCI-540) is an experimental racetam-class compound promoted as a nootropic. It was developed by Mitsubishi Tanabe Pharma, first for Alzheimer's disease, and later licensed to BrainCells Inc. for major depressive disorder and comorbid anxiety. It is not approved anywhere.
Its best-described action is enhancement of high-affinity choline uptake, a step in acetylcholine synthesis, shown in rodent models of cholinergic deficit. Sources examined do not link it to physical appearance.

name: Fasoracetam

angle.text: Fasoracetam is a never-marketed racetam that nootropic users take for focus and attention, following its trials in ADHD. It has no appearance angle tested; its place on the wiki is as part of the nootropic stack.

summary: A never-marketed racetam studied for ADHD, with no appearance evidence.
note: Investigational drug; not approved.
currentQuick:
Fasoracetam is an investigational racetam that failed in dementia trials and was then studied in ADHD and a genetic syndrome. It is sold online as a nootropic.
No source links it to appearance.
How it works: It is thought to modulate metabotropic glutamate receptors.
Risks and caveats: Not approved; side-effect information in the sources reviewed is limited to small trials.
deepLead:
Fasoracetam is an experimental racetam-class drug discovered by Nippon Shinyaku in the late 1980s and never marketed. It was tested for vascular dementia, then repurposed for ADHD and later other conditions. It appears to modulate metabotropic glutamate receptors.
It is sold online as a nootropic. Sources reviewed do not connect it to physical appearance.

name: Nefiracetam

angle.text: Nefiracetam is a Japanese racetam studied for dementia and post-stroke apathy, and nootropic users take it for memory and drive. Appearance outcomes are untested and not a stated goal.

summary: A Japanese racetam studied for dementia and post-stroke apathy, with no appearance evidence.
note: Not approved in most countries.
currentQuick:
Nefiracetam is a racetam studied for dementia and apathy after stroke. It is sold online as a nootropic.
No source links it to appearance.
How it works: Lab studies point to effects on calcium channels, acetylcholine receptors and the GABA system.
Risks and caveats: Animal toxicity (kidney, testis) was seen in dogs; human trials reported none. Prescription-only in Australia.
deepLead:
Nefiracetam (code DM-9384) is an oral racetam-class nootropic studied mainly in Japan for dementia and post-stroke apathy. It is not approved in the United States, where it is unscheduled, and it is prescription-only in Australia.
Sources reviewed do not connect it to physical appearance.

name: Sunifiram

angle.text: Sunifiram is an unapproved nootropic that users take for learning and focus, based on animal studies showing strong antiamnesic effects. There are no human trials, and no appearance use has been studied.

summary: An unapproved animal-tested nootropic with no human trials and no appearance evidence.
note: No human trials or toxicology testing.
currentQuick:
Sunifiram is an experimental nootropic developed in Italy and sold online. It is a simplified analogue of unifiram.
No source links it to appearance.
How it works: Its mechanism is unknown; research points to NMDA glycine-site and kinase pathways.
Risks and caveats: No human trials or toxicology testing have been published; unapproved in the US.
deepLead:
Sunifiram (DM-235) is an experimental nootropic from a series of piperazine compounds made by Italian researchers; it is a structural simplification of unifiram (DM-232). In animal studies it showed antiamnesic effects at much lower doses than piracetam. It has not been approved anywhere.
As of 2016, it had undergone no toxicology testing and no human trials, and sources reviewed do not connect it to physical appearance.

name: Unifiram

angle.text: Unifiram is the parent compound of sunifiram and is sold online as a potent nootropic for memory and focus. Evidence is limited to animal studies, with no human trials or appearance data.

summary: An unapproved animal-tested nootropic with no human studies and no appearance evidence.
note: No human or long-term toxicity data.
currentQuick:
Unifiram is an experimental nootropic from Italian labs, sold online. Sunifiram is derived from it.
No source links it to appearance.
How it works: Mechanism unknown; indirect AMPA pathway involvement has been suggested.
Risks and caveats: No human or long-term toxicity studies exist.
deepLead:
Unifiram (DM-232) is an experimental compound that showed antiamnesic effects in animal studies, with far greater potency than piracetam. It was developed by Italian researchers and is the parent of sunifiram. It is not patented and is sold online despite the absence of human and long-term toxicity studies.
Sources reviewed do not connect it to physical appearance.

name: Modafinil

angle.text: Forum users take modafinil to stay alert, study and work longer, and some claim it raises charisma or social ability. It is approved for sleepiness in narcolepsy, sleep apnea and shift work; the appearance and charisma claims are anecdotal and untested.

summary: Prescription wakefulness drug that forums treat as a study and productivity aid; no appearance effect has been studied.
note: Prescription-only in the US; label warns of serious rash and psychiatric symptoms.
currentQuick:
Modafinil is an FDA-approved prescription drug for excessive sleepiness from narcolepsy, sleep apnea and shift work disorder. In looksmaxxing and self-improvement forums it is discussed as a way to stay alert and productive.
No trial has tested it for appearance. Posters link it to looks only indirectly, such as appetite suppression or feeling more sociable.
How it works: The label says its mechanism is unknown. A 2009 imaging study in healthy men found it binds the dopamine transporter and raises dopamine.
Risks and caveats: The label warns of serious rash including Stevens-Johnson syndrome, hypersensitivity reactions, psychiatric symptoms and cardiovascular events. Users report headache and reduced appetite. It is prescription-only in the US.
deepLead:
Modafinil is a prescription wakefulness-promoting medication, often grouped as a eugeroic, that the US Food and Drug Administration has approved to improve wakefulness in adults with excessive sleepiness from narcolepsy, obstructive sleep apnea or shift work disorder . It was developed in France by Laboratoire Lafon and is described as a related compound to adrafinil .
The label states that the mechanism by which modafinil promotes wakefulness is unknown, and that it has wake-promoting actions similar to sympathomimetic agents such as amphetamine and methylphenidate without an identical pharmacological profile . Brain imaging work in healthy men found that it occupies the dopamine transporter and raises dopamine levels .
In looksmaxxing and wider self-improvement communities it is discussed as a productivity and study aid, sometimes grouped with other nootropics under "lifemaxxing" . No published trial has tested modafinil for any facial or physical appearance outcome. Evidence on cognitive effects in healthy people is mixed in the sources reviewed, and the drug carries labelled warnings including serious rash and psychiatric symptoms .

name: Armodafinil

angle.text: Armodafinil is the longer-acting form of modafinil and is used in the same way, for alertness and productivity in nootropic circles. It is prescribed for sleepiness, and no appearance effect has been studied.

summary: The longer-acting R-enantiomer of modafinil, prescribed for sleepiness; no appearance effect has been studied.
note: Prescription-only in the US; label warns of serious rash and hypersensitivity reactions.
currentQuick:
Armodafinil is the R-enantiomer of modafinil, approved in the US for excessive sleepiness in narcolepsy, sleep apnea and shift work disorder. In looksmaxxing forums it comes up mostly as an alternative to modafinil for staying alert.
No trial has tested it for appearance, and forum material on it is thin.
How it works: The label says the mechanism is unknown and similar to modafinil. Research reports it inhibits dopamine reuptake at the dopamine transporter.
Risks and caveats: The label warns of serious rash including Stevens-Johnson syndrome, hypersensitivity, psychiatric symptoms and cardiovascular events. It is prescription-only in the US.
deepLead:
Armodafinil is the R-enantiomer of modafinil and a prescription wakefulness-promoting medication. The US label lists it to improve wakefulness in adults with excessive sleepiness associated with obstructive sleep apnea, narcolepsy or shift work disorder, and specifies that in sleep apnea it treats sleepiness and not the underlying obstruction . Grokipedia gives the brand name as Nuvigil and a 2007 US approval .
As with modafinil, the label says the mechanism of wake promotion is unknown, with properties similar to modafinil in animal and in vitro tests . A 2012 study found the R-enantiomer to be a dopamine uptake inhibitor with properties that may differ from the racemic mixture .
Armodafinil is mentioned in looksmaxxing communities mainly in comparison with modafinil as a study and productivity aid. No published trial has tested it for any appearance outcome, and the available looksmax.org material about it is limited to passing comparisons.

name: Adrafinil

angle.text: Adrafinil is a modafinil prodrug that users take as an over-the-counter route to the same wakefulness for study and work. It was sold in France for vigilance in older adults, human data are thin, and no appearance use has been studied.

summary: A modafinil prodrug once sold in France; no appearance use has been studied and human data are thin.
note: Not FDA-approved; withdrawn from the French market in 2011 per Grokipedia.
currentQuick:
Adrafinil is converted by the liver into modafinil. It was sold in France as Olmifon for sleepiness and inattention in older adults until 2011 and is not approved in the US.
No published trial has tested it for appearance outcomes, and little human clinical research exists.
How it works: It is a prodrug: the liver metabolises it to modafinil, which acts on the dopamine transporter.
Risks and caveats: Human safety data are limited in the sources reviewed. It is listed as a stimulant in doping control and is not approved for any use in the US.
deepLead:
Adrafinil is a wakefulness-promoting compound that the body converts to modafinil. According to Grokipedia, it was developed by Laboratoire Lafon in France, marketed there as Olmifon from the mid-1980s for vigilance problems in older adults, and withdrawn by its manufacturer in 2011 .
Because it is a precursor of modafinil, its effects are attributed to that metabolite, which acts on the dopamine transporter . Adrafinil is not approved by the US Food and Drug Administration for any use and is sold outside prescription channels in some markets as a supplement or research chemical, per Grokipedia . It is also on doping-control lists as a stimulant, and chemists have published methods to detect it .
No published human trial has tested adrafinil for any appearance outcome. The sources reviewed contain no looksmaxxing forum material about it, so its place in appearance culture is not documented here beyond its relation to modafinil.

name: Citicoline (CDP-choline)

angle.text: Citicoline is a choline source taken as a nootropic for focus and memory. It is studied for stroke and brain injury, and no trial tests it for appearance.

summary: A choline-donor nootropic studied for stroke and brain injury; no trial tests it for appearance.
note: Large stroke and brain-injury trials did not show overall benefit.
currentQuick:
Citicoline is a naturally occurring nucleotide that supplies choline and cytidine for membrane synthesis. It is sold as a supplement in the US and used as a drug in some countries for stroke and cognitive decline.
No trial has tested it for appearance, and it is not discussed in the looksmaxxing sources reviewed.
How it works: After ingestion it is broken down into choline and cytidine, which the brain uses to make phosphatidylcholine, a membrane phospholipid.
Risks and caveats: Grokipedia describes a good safety profile at therapeutic amounts. The large ICTUS and COBRIT trials did not show benefit in stroke or brain injury.
deepLead:
Citicoline, or cytidine 5'-diphosphocholine (CDP-choline), is a nucleotide that occurs naturally in the body as an intermediate in the synthesis of phosphatidylcholine, a membrane phospholipid . It is sold as a prescription drug in some countries for stroke and cognitive disorders and as a dietary supplement in others, including the United States, according to Grokipedia .
It is marketed as a cholinergic nootropic. Large randomised trials in acute ischaemic stroke and traumatic brain injury, notably ICTUS and COBRIT, did not show the benefit seen in earlier smaller studies, while pooled analyses of earlier trials had suggested a benefit .
No published trial has tested citicoline for any appearance outcome, and the sources reviewed contain no looksmaxxing community discussion of it.

name: Alpha-GPC

angle.text: Alpha-GPC is sold as a cognitive and sports supplement, with lifters using it for focus and training output that could support muscle gain. It is a prescription drug for cognitive decline in Italy, and no appearance outcome has been studied.

summary: A choline donor sold as a cognitive and sports supplement; no appearance outcome has been studied.
note: Human evidence is mainly older Italian studies in stroke and dementia; one 2024 trial lists growth hormone as an outcome.
currentQuick:
Alpha-GPC is a choline-containing compound used as a supplement, and as a prescription drug in some countries, to support acetylcholine synthesis. Older Italian trials studied it in stroke and dementia, and newer ones in cognition and athletic performance.
No trial has tested it for appearance, and it does not appear in the looksmaxxing sources reviewed.
How it works: It supplies choline, a precursor of acetylcholine and of membrane phospholipids; rat studies reported raised hippocampal acetylcholine.
Risks and caveats: Grokipedia reports low adverse event rates in older Italian trials; detailed safety data are limited in the sources reviewed. It is sold as a supplement in the US and is not FDA-approved as a drug.
deepLead:
Alpha-GPC (L-alpha-glycerylphosphorylcholine, or choline alfoscerate) is a choline-containing compound that serves as a source of choline for the synthesis of the neurotransmitter acetylcholine and for cell membrane phospholipids . According to Grokipedia, it is a prescription drug in some countries such as Italy for cognitive decline and is sold as a dietary supplement in the United States, where a 2012 GRAS notice addressed its use as a choline source .
Most published human research dates from Italian multicentre studies in the 1990s in stroke, transient ischaemic attacks and dementia . More recent registered trials have examined it for cognition and athletic performance in healthy adults .
No published study has tested alpha-GPC for facial or body appearance outcomes, and the sources reviewed contain no looksmaxxing forum discussion of it.
